subject.title: Add backup/restore utility for config, cron jobs, and session history

question: Should OpenClaw core own a safe local instance restore command over its existing backup archives, while delegating cloud storage, recurring schedules, retention, and provider-specific encryption to plugins?
rationale: Source establishes that create/verify is intentionally first-party, but neither current code nor discussion defines which state is restorable, how destructive conflicts and secrets are handled, or where optional cloud lifecycle features belong.

options.title: Native local restore only
options.body: Specify and implement a security-reviewed local restore lifecycle over verified OpenClaw archives, leaving cloud and scheduling integrations to plugins.

options.title: Keep manual restoration
options.body: Document a supported manual restore procedure and continue hardening archive verification without adding a destructive native restore command.

options.title: Full core backup service
options.body: Adopt restore, scheduling, retention, encryption, and cloud backends as a broad core subsystem with corresponding configuration and long-term ownership.

recommendation.title: Native local restore only
recommendation.body: Specify and implement a security-reviewed local restore lifecycle over verified OpenClaw archives, leaving cloud and scheduling integrations to plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest product-routing comments already identify the unresolved native scope and safety questions, making this the strongest available decision-owner signal.
